items.title: Perlis Good Samaritan killed while assisting auxiliary policeman in earlier accident
items.summary: ARAU, Aug 4 — A factory operator was killed after being hit by a skidding car while trying to assist an Universiti Malaysia Perlis (UniMAP) auxiliary policeman who had been involved in an earlier accident along Jalan Kuala Perlis-Changlun, Sungai Chempa here this morning. Arau District Police Chief Supt Ahmad Mohsin Md Rodi said that the 39-year-old male victim died at the scene, while the driver of the Perodua Axia – a 35-year-old female doctor – and the 36-year-old male auxiliary policeman both sustained severe injuries. “Prior to that, the factory operator wanted to help the UniMAP auxiliary policeman who had been involved in an accident, where the Honda City driven by the auxiliary policeman had skidded to the left side of the road and hit a tree after hydroplaning on water standing on the road,” he said in a statement today.

items.title: Foreign man arrested over alleged assault, intimidation of student
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Police have arrested a foreign man suspected of assaulting and criminally intimidating a local student at a residential area in Sungai Besi. Cheras police chief Assistant Commissioner Mohd Rosdi Daud said the suspect, a 39-year-old man who works as a composer, was detained during a raid at a condominium unit here at about 1.51am on July 26. He said the arrest was carried out by a team from the Cheras police headquarters' Criminal Investigation Department (D7), acting on intelligence.

items.title: Ringgit eases versus US dollar, ends higher against other major currencies
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit ended lower against the US dollar although it strengthened versus other major currencies on Tuesday, as the greenback remained supported by stronger-than-expected US manufacturing data. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the US dollar is likely to remain well supported as positive economic data from the United States reinforces confidence in the strength of the US economy. Nevertheless, Mohd Afzanizam said, the ringgit was mostly flat versus the US dollar and moved within a narrow range throughout the day.

items.title: LTAT stresses prudent management of military personnel savings
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Armed Forces Fund Board (LTAT) has reaffirmed its commitment to safeguarding the savings of about 117,000 military personnel and delivering sustainable long-term returns. Its chief executive Mohammad Ashraf Md Radzi said LTAT bore a significant responsibility as the contributions entrusted to it belonged to armed forces personnel who had devoted the prime years of their lives to serving the country. Also present from Media Prima were Media Prima Content, TV Networks and Primeworks Studios chief executive officer Nini Yusof; Media Prima Audio chief executive officer Nazri Noran; Media Prima Omnia chief operating officer (Direct Solutions) Datuk Mohd Efendi Omar; and Big Tree chief operating officer Muhamad Fariz Mustafa.

items.title: Employers under probe after 49 workers checked in Pangkor op
items.summary: Perak Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA) director Maritime Captain Mohamad Shukri Khotob said in a statement today that the operation was carried out in collaboration with the Perak Labour Department, involving 37 personnel from both agencies. "The inspection found that several employers are suspected of committing various labour law violations, including failing to notify the Labour Office of the hiring of foreign workers within 14 days from the date of hiring as stipulated under the Employment Act 1955," he said. He said the integrated operations focused on inspecting fishing premises to ensure compliance with labour laws, detecting elements of human trafficking, and combating labour exploitation, particularly involving foreign workers.

items.title: Michigan primary offers key test of Democratic voters' views on Israel
items.summary: MICHIGAN voters head to the polls on Tuesday in a high-stakes Democratic Senate primary that could shape the battle for control of Congress and the future of the Democratic Party amid a fierce internal debate over US support for Israel. The contest pits Abdul El-Sayed, a progressive former public health official who wants to end unconditional US military aid to Israel and accuses it of genocide, against US Representative Haley Stevens, a moderate backed by pro-Israel groups and a longtime outspoken supporter of Israel. The outcome could offer the clearest signal yet of whether Democratic voters are more receptive to an anti-establishment message hostile to Israel and big money in politics, or a more moderate approach supportive of Israel, according to analysts and party strategists interviewed by Reuters.

items.title: Second Malaysian in a week arrested for drug smuggling in Indonesia
items.summary: JAKARTA, Aug 4 — Another Malaysian has been arrested in Indonesia within days for allegedly attempting to smuggle nearly one kilogramme of methamphetamine and more than 1,000 ecstasy pills concealed beneath a corset into Indonesia through Juanda International Airport in East Java. Juanda Naval Air Base (Lanudal Juanda) Commander Col Henoch Nasarius Virzawan said the 22-year-old suspect was arrested after customs officers acted on information on the morning of July 29 that a passenger arriving from Kuala Lumpur was suspected of carrying narcotics. Henoch attributed the interception to close coordination among naval security, customs, immigration, airport security and other agencies at Juanda Airport, adding that the Indonesian Navy would continue strengthening cooperation with airport authorities to tighten security and prevent drug smuggling by air.

items.title: Providers must verify age via MyKad or passport under new social media rules
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Licensed social media service providers must now implement official document verification, including MyKad or passports, to ensure account holders are aged 16 and above. "The MCMC has issued written notices under Subsection 30(2) of the Online Safety Act 2025 (Act 866) to social media service providers, requiring them to explain instances of non-compliance and the measures taken to implement age verification mechanisms," the ministry said. On online scams, paid advertisements, and fake accounts, the ministry said MCMC submitted 292,102 takedown requests between Jan 1, 2022, and July 31, 2026, with 279,875 items (96 per cent) removed.

items.title: 1,404 vessels on watchlist as govt tightens screening of sanctioned ships
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The government has strengthened its vessel monitoring and screening mechanisms to prevent ships listed under international sanctions from entering Malaysian waters and ports. "To prevent vessels on international sanctions lists from entering Malaysian waters through ship renaming, reflagging, or changes in ownership, the government has implemented several control mechanisms. Regarding Israeli vessels, the ministry said that on Dec 20, 2023, the government banned Israeli-registered ships from docking at Malaysian ports; prohibited ships flying the Israeli flag from entering Malaysian ports; and revoked the operating permission of Israeli shipping company ZIM Integrated Shipping Services Ltd.

items.title: Healthcare, financial services lift Bursa Malaysia higher at the close
items.summary: Among the heavyweights, Maybank slid six sen to RM10.78, Public Bank gained eight sen to RM5.28, CIMB Group added two sen to RM8.03, IHH Healthcare climbed 13 sen to RM8.43, and Tenaga Nasional was flat at RM14.50. As for the most active stocks, Zetrix AI was one sen higher at 73.5 sen, Mr D.I.Y. dropped 10 sen to RM1.52, NationGate Holdings put on six sen to RM1.29, HHRG was unchanged at 11.5 sen, and Dataprep Holdings was one sen lower to six sen.

items.title: US has used 'virtually all' of its long-range precision missiles during Iran war
items.summary: NEW YORK: The US Army has used up much of its stockpile of highly accurate long-range missiles during its five-month war with Iran, according to three people familiar with the data, raising concerns about the military's readiness for future conflicts. The missiles are principally the Army's surface-to-surface weapons, known as Army Tactical Missile Systems (ATACMS) and Precision Strike Missiles (PrSM). The US has used "virtually all" of these weapons, according to two of the sources.

items.title: Security expert: Malaysian pilot arrested in Jakarta jeopardised lives by flying 'high'
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The arrest of a Malaysia Airlines pilot in Indonesia for alleged drug smuggling is a wake-up call for the entire aviation industry, not just the national carrier. National Defence University of Malaysia (UPNM) Professor Dr Mohd Mizan Mohammad Aslam said the case was particularly alarming because the pilot was not merely smuggling drugs — he had also been under the influence of narcotics while operating a passenger flight. Mizan called for two key long-term reforms.

items.title: CAAM seeks public, industry feedback on Low Altitude Economy framework
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia (CAAM) has invited industry players, government agencies, academia and members of the public to submit feedback by Sept 2 on a proposed national framework that will chart the country's Low Altitude Economy (LAE). CAAM chief executive officer Datuk Captain Norazman Mahmud said the proposed Malaysia LAE Framework is aimed at providing the country's long-term strategic direction for developing a safe, secure, sustainable and commercially viable low-altitude aviation ecosystem. Norazman said the public consultation represents an important step in translating Malaysia's LAE ambitions into a coordinated and implementable national framework "Malaysia has the industrial capabilities, talent and technological foundations to build a competitive LAE.

items.title: HLB bags six regional, international awards in wealth management
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Hong Leong Bank Bhd (HLB) has clinched six regional and international wealth management awards, with its HLB Private Bank and HLB Priority businesses recognised for their offerings to high-net-worth and emerging affluent clients. HLB Private Bank was named Best Private Bank/Wealth Manager in Malaysia and Singapore at the WealthBriefingAsia Awards, while HLB Priority won Best Bank/Wealth Manager for Emerging Affluent Clients at the Global Mass Affluent Banking Awards. HLB Private also received the Rising Star Private Bank Award for Malaysia and Best Private Bank for Wealth Creation & Preservation at the Global Private Banking Innovation Awards.

items.title: Tony Pua denies stake in tech firm awarded Tabung Haji project
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 4 — DAP’s Tony Pua has rejected alleged links to a tech company that secured a RM4.53 million contract with Tabung Haji (TH) in 2019, saying he held no shares in the firm at the time of the award. The former Damansara MP said that he had sold his shares in Cyber Village Sdn Bhd (CVSB) back in 2007, FMT reported. “I have absolutely nothing to do with the award (given by TH to CVSB),” Pua said..

items.title: 149 state food production zones gazetted
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A total of 149 out of 176 permanent food production zones under state government jurisdiction have been gazetted to date, said Deputy Agriculture and Food Security Minister Datuk Chan Foong Hin. He said the Agriculture and Food Security Ministry, through the Agriculture Department, the Department of Veterinary Services (DVS) and the Fisheries Department (DOF), stands ready to collaborate with state governments to identify, develop and gazette potential areas, including suburban areas. "All Permanent Food Production Parks (TKPM), Permanent Ruminant Production Parks (TKPR) and Aquaculture Industrial Zone (ZIA) projects are regulated by the three departments.

items.title: Stratus surges to record high on growing interest in semicon automation
items.summary: The stock closed 21 sen, or 10 per cent, higher at RM2.31, with more than 14.7 million shares traded. Stratus Global has been among the market's strongest-performing initial public offerings this year. The firm forecasts Stratus Global to post core net profit of RM69.7 million in FY27 and RM84.8 million in FY28.

items.title: 46 accidents, 11 deaths during RXZ Members 8.0 programme
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A total of 46 road accident cases involving motorcyclists were recorded in a four-day period starting from July 30 to last Sunday, during the RXZ Members 8.0 programme. Bukit Aman Traffic Enforcement and Investigation Department (TEID) director Datuk Seri Muhammed Hasbullah Ali said that of the total, 11 cases or 23.91 per cent were fatal accidents, five cases (10.87 per cent) were serious accidents and 30 cases (65.22 per cent) were minor accidents. According to the daily breakdown, four cases were recorded on July 30, 16 cases on July 31, 11 cases on Aug 1 and 15 cases Aug 2 involving a total of 44 male and two female victims, he said.

items.title: Suhakam expresses deep concern after appeals court upholds stay on Pastor Koh probe
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Human Rights Commission of Malaysia (Suhakam) has expressed deep concern over the Court of Appeal's decision to uphold a stay of the High Court's orders in the enforced disappearance case of Pastor Raymond Koh. The High Court ruled on Nov 5, 2025, in favour of Pastor Koh's family, finding the Malaysian government and police liable for his abduction and enforced disappearance in 2017. However, on Jan 26, the Court of Appeal stayed the High Court order requiring police to recommence investigations into his disappearance.

items.title: Lula, Brazil's political titan, races against time
items.summary: SHIRTLESS and drenched in sweat on his treadmill, Lula runs. At 80, President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, the dominant figure in Brazilian politics for four decades, wants to show he still has the energy to win a fourth term in office in October's election. The leftist leader has survived electoral defeats, 580 days in prison, and the disgrace of a corruption conviction which, although later annulled, still prompts taunts from the right of "Lula the thief."

items.title: Police: 11 deaths and 46 accidents from four days of RXZ Members 8.0
items.summary: Bukit Aman Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Department (JSPT) director Datuk Seri Muhammed Hasbullah Ali said that of the total, 11 cases or 23.91 per cent were fatal accidents, five cases (10.87 per cent) were serious accidents and 30 cases (65.22 per cent) were minor accidents. He said that according to the daily breakdown, four cases were recorded on July 30, 16 cases (July 31), 11 cases (August 1) and 15 cases (August 2) involving a total of 44 male and two female victims. Muhammed Hasbullah said JSPT takes the number of fatal and serious accidents seriously, especially involving young motorcyclists seriously.

items.title: Tabung Haji RCI: Design firm director arrested over RM300,000 ‘renovation bribes’
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 4 — A design firm director has been taken into custody for allegedly funding lavish home renovations worth RM300,000 for a statutory body’s former chief operating officer (COO) as a kickback to secure lucrative projects. The suspect, a man in his 50s, was nabbed at 7.30pm yesterday while recording a statement at the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) headquarters. MACC chief Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman confirmed the arrest when contacted.

items.title: Negri Sembilan DAP to focus solely on unity government motion
items.summary: SEREMBAN: Negri Sembilan DAP will focus solely on the central leadership's motion on whether the party should remain in the unity government until the end of the parliamentary term at its national congress on Aug 16. State DAP secretary Cha Kee Chin said the chapter would not submit any additional motions at the annual congress. Our focus is strictly on the single motion from the central leadership to decide whether DAP will remain in the unity government or otherwise," he said when contacted today.

items.title: IRB raises RM4.4b in additional tax assessments as of June 30
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Inland Revenue Board (IRB) has raised RM4.4 billion in additional tax assessments as of June 30, said its chief executive officer Datuk Dr Abu Tariq Jamaluddin. He said this reflects IRB's commitment to protecting the country's revenue and strengthening the integrity of the taxation system. "The IRB focuses on implementing strategic risk-based audit and compliance activities to detect and address significant cases of non-compliance, including tax evasion and aggressive tax planning.

items.title: Lebanon's negotiations with Israel bring 'shame and humiliation': Hizbollah
items.summary: BEIRUT: Hizbollah leader Naim Qassem said on Tuesday that direct negotiations between Lebanon and Israel would bring "nothing but shame, humiliation, and successive compromises" for Lebanon, ahead of new talks in Rome. In a televised address, Qassem said Lebanon's President Joseph Aoun "has not acted as an arbiter, nor as a unifying figure, but has become biased and divisive, which is incompatible with his role and with Lebanon's strength." In another matter, Qassem said Tuesday that he had no objection to meeting with Syria's leadership, the first time he has expressed such a stance, after his Iran-backed group fought for Syria's former authorities that were ousted in 2024.

items.title: 5-year-old survivor of Bentong tree crash in stable condition
items.summary: Pahang Health director Dr Saiful Azlan Sharif said Muhammad Rizz Haziq Mohd Radzi, who suffered minor injuries to his face and head, was receiving treatment at the hospital and remained in stable condition. The incident claimed the lives of his father, Maran Umno Youth chief Mohd Radzi Rahimi; mother Nuraini Mohammad Jafri, 36; twin brother Muhammad Rizz Hazim; and uncle Mohammad Nizam Mohammad Jafri, 35. Meanwhile, Radzi's father, Rahimi Abd Samad, 63, said the family had yet to decide who would care for Rizz Haziq.

items.title: Termite infestation blamed for heritage shophouse collapse in Penang
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: A termite-damaged wooden beam caused the collapse at a heritage shophouse in Lebuh Armenian, injuring two Sri Lankan tourists today. State Local Government and Town and Country Planning Committee chairman Jason H'ng said inspections found the building's wooden beam had deteriorated after being infested by termites before it gave way. "The area is a heritage site, but the buildings are still privately owned.

items.title: 4 teachers testify in Bandar Utama school murder trial
items.summary: SHAH ALAM: Four teachers took the witness stand today in the murder trial of a 15-year-old boy, giving evidence about the events that unfolded inside SMK Bandar Utama Damansara (4) on the day of the fatal stabbing incident last year. The boy's lawyer, Kitson Foong, who briefed the media on the closed-door proceedings, said the teachers' testimony focused on what happened in and around the school toilet before continuing with events in the school compound. The teachers were Nursyazwani Saari, Syaza Sahira Abdul Jalil, Muhammad Alif Abdul Razak and Mohd Qauyyum Firdaus Juhar.

items.title: More remains found at second Kosovo mass grave
items.summary: PRISTINA: Kosovo authorities confirmed late Monday that the remains of four people were found at a second mass grave in the country's north, as investigations into a suspected 1990s war crime continue. The discovery comes days after the remains of seven people were uncovered at a nearby dig site in the area of Zubin Potok – with officials believing there could be as many as 23 people buried near surrounding villages. "During excavations conducted in Jabuka, the mortal remains of four people were found and exhumed, who, according to initial assessments, belong to victims of enforced disappearance during the war," the Government Commission on Missing Persons announced in a press release.

items.title: Bukit Aman to probe second Malaysian drug arrest in Indonesia
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Bukit Aman has begun looking into the arrest of another Malaysian in Indonesia over alleged drug trafficking, just a few days after a Malaysia Airlines pilot was detained in Jakarta on similar allegations. Federal Narcotics Crime Investigation Department director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan confirmed that police would follow up on the latest case involving a 22-year-old Malaysian from Johor who was arrested at Juanda International Airport in Surabaya. According to Indonesian news portal Jakarta Globe, authorities discovered four packages containing 990g of methamphetamine and another four packages containing 1,089 ecstasy pills strapped beneath a corset worn around the suspect's body.

items.title: Sabah, Petronas launch digital platforms to strengthen oil and gas workforce
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU: The Sabah state government has partnered with Petronas to strengthen the state's oil and gas workforce through the development of two online platforms aimed at improving access to employment, training and work pass services. The national oil company funded the Permohonan Online Pekerjaan dan Latihan Dalam Industri Minyak dan Gas (Pomigas) and the Sabah Work Pass Online System, both managed by the Chief Minister's Department's Home Affairs and Research Office. Pomigas began operations earlier this year, while the Sabah Work Pass Online System will be operational from Sept 1.

items.title: Ukraine will never join Nato, former top commander says
items.summary: KYIV: Ukraine's ex-army chief Valery Zaluzhny has said the country, fighting a Russian invasion since 2022, will "never" join Nato despite Kyiv's stated intention to become a member of the US-led military alliance. "I know Nato very well. "Unfortunately, we never will," added Zaluzhny, currently the Ukrainian ambassador to Britain.

items.title: Penang launches campaign to boost domestic tourism
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: Penang has launched its "Fall in Love with Penang" campaign to encourage Malaysians to rediscover the state and sustain visitor arrivals through the year-end. State Tourism and Creative Economy Committee chairman Wong Hon Wai said the campaign marked a shift in strategy to strengthen the domestic market while continuing efforts to attract international visitors. He said while Penang had continued promoting itself overseas, the state was now balancing its strategy by placing greater emphasis on domestic tourism.

items.title: Modernise tax system to stay competitive: Amir Hamzah
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia must modernise its tax system to keep pace with an increasingly digital and interconnected global economy, ensuring the country remains competitive, attracts investment and strengthens its fiscal resilience. Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan said shifting business models, expanding cross-border transactions and evolving international tax rules required the government to continually refine its tax policy and administration. "New business models, cross-border transactions and developments in international taxation require governments to continuously modernise their approach to tax policy and administration," he said when officiating the 26th National Tax Conference here today.

items.title: MACC detains former estate manager over RM8m rubber sapling supply probe linked to Tabung Haji RCI
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 4 — The former estate manager of a rubber sapling supply company in the Klang Valley has been detained by the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) on suspicion of misappropriating a sapling supply contract worth approximately RM8 million. Sources said that the man in his 50s, who is suspected of embezzling the sapling supply contract intended for a subsidiary of a statutory body involved in the plantation sector, was arrested at 7:00 pm yesterday while present to give a statement at the MACC Headquarters here. He is believed to have misappropriated the rubber sapling supply project across two plantation companies - subsidiaries of a statutory body - involving contracts worth approximately RM8 million,” the source said.

items.title: LRT3 article sparks RM100m defamation suit by MRCB, vice-chairman against journalist
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 4 — Malaysian Resources Corporation Bhd (MRCB) and executive vice-chairman Salim Fateh Din have reportedly filed a RM100 million lawsuit against journalist P. Gunasegaram over an article on the LRT3 Shah Alam Line. The suit also alleged that the article linked MRCB to the project’s cost increases and delays, and implied that Salim relied on political ties to obtain business benefits for the company. MRCB and Salim reportedly claimed the article damaged their reputation and credibility, causing a loss in confidence among investors and business partners and negatively affected MRCB’s share price.

items.title: Beauty therapist claims loan sharks demanded RM16k over RM6k loan
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A 30-year-old beauty therapist has sought help from MCA Public Services and Complaints Department head Datuk Seri Michael Chong after alleged loan sharks demanded RM16,000 to settle a RM6,000 loan. She said she borrowed a total of RM6,000 from two alleged loan sharks — RM5,000 from one lender and RM1,000 from another. "I wanted to settle the loan.

items.title: Social media age verification rules in force since June 1, says Communications Ministry
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 4 (Bernama) -- Licensed social media service providers are now required to implement age verification mechanisms using official documents, such as MyKad or passports, to ensure that only individuals aged 16 and above can register for and hold accounts on their platforms. “The MCMC has issued written notices under Subsection 30(2) of the Online Safety Act 2025 (Act 866) to social media service providers, requiring them to explain instances of non-compliance and the measures taken to implement age verification mechanisms,” the ministry said. On enforcement against online scams involving paid advertisements, fake accounts, and harmful online content, the ministry said the MCMC submitted 292,102 takedown requests between Jan 1, 2022, and July 31, 2026, with 279,875 items, or 96 per cent, successfully removed.

items.title: Health reforms must be guided by evidence-based data, says Dzulkefly
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 4 — The implementation of health reforms must be guided by accurate, evidence-based data to ensure policies effectively strengthen Malaysia’s healthcare ecosystem, Health Minister Datuk Seri Dzulkefly Ahmad said. This philosophy strongly underpins the Ministry of Health’s (MOH) health reform agenda. Instead, we are implementing meaningful reforms that include comprehensive healthcare digitalisation, sustainable health financing, and safeguarding the welfare of our frontline workforce,” he said.

items.title: Plantation brawl in Port Dickson leaves three foreign workers dead, one injured
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Aug 4 — Three foreign labourers were killed while another was injured in a fight at Taman Linggi, Port Dickson, yesterday evening. Negeri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad said his department received information from the public at about 4.15 pm about a fight involving Bangladeshi labourers who were colleagues at a plantation in the district. “Upon receiving information, a police team from the Linggi police station rushed to the scene of the incident and arrested a fellow Malaysian man in his 40s who was suspected of being involved.

items.title: Sarawak needs more dietitians to promote balanced nutrition, says Abang Johari
items.summary: KUCHING, Aug 4 — Sarawak needs more professional dietetic experts to ensure balanced meals in daily nutrition, said Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg. He said that the presence of professional dietitians is important to help the community understand the nutritional content of food and to plan meals that meet dietary needs. “We need many professional dietetic experts so that the food we serve is balanced from a dietary perspective.

items.title: Mukhriz’s challenge against RM5m IRB tax notices gets Nov 16 decision date
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 4 — The High Court today fixed Nov 16 to deliver its decision on a judicial review application filed by Datuk Seri Mukhriz Mahathir challenging the Inland Revenue Board's (IRB) issuance of Notices of Additional Assessment totalling more than RM5 million for the 2017 to 2019 assessment years. Judge Datuk Azizan Md Arshad set the date after hearing submissions from lawyer Nizamuddin Abdul Hamid, representing Mukhriz, and Senior Revenue Counsel Marina Ibrahim, appearing for the Director-General of the Inland Revenue Board. On Jan 2, 2025, the High Court granted Mukhriz leave to commence the judicial review proceedings.

items.title: Foreign Ministry tracking 21,427 Malaysians in conflict-hit countries for possible evacuation
items.summary: Deputy Foreign Minister Datuk Lukanisman Awang Sauni said experience in handling previous conflicts had helped the government strengthen its preparedness. Lukanisman said Petroliam Nasional Bhd (Petronas) also had its own plan to evacuate its employees. Responding to Musoddak’s original question on the plan to protect Malaysians in the Middle East, including Umrah pilgrims, Lukanisman said all Malaysian diplomatic missions have a contingency plan that is constantly updated, including mapping the location of Malaysians, communication mechanisms, resource coordination and evacuation strategies.

items.title: Perak Sultan opens Manjung Municipal Council’s new Merdeka Hall
items.summary: LUMUT, Aug 4 — The Sultan of Perak, Sultan Nazrin Shah, today opened the Merdeka Hall of the Manjung Municipal Council here. The Raja Permaisuri of Perak, Tuanku Zara Salim, and the Raja Di Hilir of Perak, Raja Iskandar Dzurkarnain Sultan Idris Shah also attended the event. In his speech, Saarani said the opening of the hall marked three closely linked milestones.

items.title: Police arrest three after missing Johor man found dead in river
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Aug 4 — Police have arrested three men to assist in the investigation into the discovery of a man’s body in Sungai Tanjung Sembrong, Parit Raja, Batu Pahat, yesterday. Deputy Johor police chief Hoo Chuan Huat said the victim was found wrapped in a fishing net, with his hands and feet tied with adhesive tape and injuries on his body. He said the discovery of the victim’s body was reported by the public at 12.30pm yesterday.

items.title: AI training using copyrighted works requires owners’ approval, says deputy minister
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 4 — The use of copyrighted material for artificial intelligence (AI) model training is subject to approval from copyright holders, with licensing arrangements and royalty payments to be agreed by the relevant parties under the Copyright Act 1987. Deputy Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Minister Datuk Fuziah Salleh said the requirement applies to any use of copyrighted works, whether for AI applications or other purposes. Fuziah said Section 27 of the Copyright Act 1987 stipulates that payment arrangements are subject to agreements between parties, which can be carried out through licensing, rights assignments or managed through Collective Management Organisations (CMOs) representing copyright owners.

items.title: Drug seizures at KLIA jump nearly six-fold as syndicates target airport
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Aug 4 — Federal narcotics police said today that drug syndicates may be favouring Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) as a transit hub because flights from the airport are not prioritised for security screening over those from other regional airports. Bukit Aman Narcotics Crime Investigation Department director Commissioner Datuk Hussein Omar Khan, however, said the number of arrests and drug seizures indicated that KLIA remained a preferred transit point for syndicates attempting to smuggle drugs overseas. “The estimated value of the drugs seized in 2026 is RM108.35 million, compared with RM18.46 million last year,” he said.

items.title: How did a Malaysia Airlines pilot’s drug-filled baggage clear KLIA? Police identify person of interest
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Aug 4 — Federal police said today they have identified a person of interest in their investigation into how a Malaysian pilot arrested with drugs at an Indonesian airport passed through security screening at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) without his baggage being flagged. Bukit Aman Narcotics Crime Investigation Department director Commissioner Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said the person of interest is an airport employee in his 30s who was assigned to the security screening area through which the pilot passed. Citing Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS) director-general Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain, Hussein said the pilot’s baggage was not flagged as high risk and was cleared under existing standard operating procedures without undergoing a secondary inspection.

items.title: Govt eyes levy on EVs to close gap in public charging infrastructure
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 4 — The government is considering imposing a levy on every electric vehicle (EV) sold to establish a fund for expanding Malaysia’s public EV charging network, Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani said. Johari said the government had previously granted exemptions on import duty, excise duty and sales tax for completely built-up (CBU) EVs for four years to spur market growth and attract investment. “After four years, when we looked for public charging stations, the investment from EV industry players was simply not there,” he said.

items.title: Sabah proposes tourism be placed under Concurrent List in line with MA63
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Aug 4 — The Sabah state government has proposed for tourism to be placed under the Concurrent List of the Federal Constitution, in line with the Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63). State Tourism, Culture and Environment Minister Datuk Jafry Ariffin said the proposal is not intended to separate Sabah from the national tourism framework, but rather to establish a more effective operational partnership between the federal and state governments. “Sabah’s unique biodiversity, extensive protected areas, island tourism, and indigenous heritage require tailored policies that address the state’s specific geographical and socio-economic realities,” he said in a statement today.

items.title: Mother’s desperate attempts to save son fail in Kuala Terengganu fire
items.summary: KUALA TERENGGANU, Aug 4 — A mother was overcome with regret after failing to save her son who was trapped in a fire that destroyed their home in here last night. Sharipah Yusof, 59, said she tried three times to brave the flames and enter the house to rescue her son, Abd Latif Abd Rashid, 41, who was sleeping in a locked room upstairs when the incident occurred at 10.52 pm. “The person told us the house was on fire and pulled us out.

items.title: Negeri Sembilan considers creating Deputy Exco positions, says MB
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Aug 4 — The Negeri Sembilan government is considering a proposal to create Deputy Executive Council (Exco) positions for several portfolios as part of efforts to strengthen the state administration, said Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim. He said Exco positions would be filled by several state assemblymen from Barisan Nasional (BN) component parties, PAS and Parti Wawasan Negara (Wawasan). “There may not be enough Exco posts to offer, so we are considering creating Deputy Exco positions for several portfolios that I believe are important,” he told reporters at Wisma Negeri here today.

items.title: Suhakam: Further delay in Pastor Raymond Koh case could jeopardise crucial evidence, witnesses
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 4 — The Human Rights Commission of Malaysia (Suhakam) today warned that the Court of Appeal’s decision last week to keep parts of the High Court’s ruling in Pastor Raymond Koh’s disappearance case on hold could further delay the search for truth and accountability. In November 2025, the High Court found the government and police liable for Koh’s enforced disappearance and ordered the investigation to be reopened under several conditions. Suhakam’s 2019 public inquiry had earlier concluded that Koh, who disappeared in February 2017, was the victim of an enforced disappearance carried out by state agents.

items.title: Teenage students killed after motorcycle crashes near Temerloh
items.summary: KUANTAN, Aug 4 — Two 17-year-old school students were killed in a three-vehicle crash at KM119 of Jalan Kuala Lumpur-Kuantan near Temerloh yesterday. Temerloh district police chief ACP Mohd Nasyim Bahron said police were alerted to the crash involving a motorcyclist and his pillion rider at 8.20 pm. He said initial investigations indicated the victims were travelling from Temerloh town towards Chenor in Maran at the time of the crash.

items.title: Pulau Burung landfill fire extinguished after nearly four-hour operation
items.summary: NIBONG TEBAL, Aug 4 — The Penang Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) took nearly four hours to fully extinguish a landfill fire at the Pulau Burung Solid Waste Disposal Site here last night. Its Fire and Rescue Operations Division assistant director John Sagun Francis said a team from the Nibong Tebal Fire and Rescue Station (BBP) was sent to the scene after receiving an emergency call at 8.14 pm. The fire involved an area measuring 120 feet by 90 feet, with the operation commander conducting an initial assessment before directing firefighters to contain and extinguish the blaze, including building a fire break to prevent it from spreading.

items.title: MACC arrests five more immigration officers over alleged MyIMMs hacking
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 4 — The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) has arrested five more immigration officers for allegedly colluding in hacking the Malaysian Immigration System (MyIMMs) to facilitate the unlawful processing and approval of Temporary Employment Visit Passes (PLKS). “Following the arrests, the MACC seized five mobile phones belonging to the suspects,” the source said. On July 28, the MACC arrested 12 individuals, including six immigration officers, in a joint operation conducted with several other agencies across the Klang Valley and Penang.

items.title: Anwar praises Malaysian contingent’s fighting spirit at Glasgow Commonwealth Games
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 4 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has congratulated the entire Malaysian contingent for their fighting spirit and commendable performances at the 2026 Glasgow Commonwealth Games. In a Facebook post last night, he also expressed appreciation to the coaches, officials, support staff and all Malaysians who continuously prayed for the success of the national contingent. “Alhamdulillah, my heartfelt congratulations to the entire Malaysian contingent for competing with great pride and displaying extraordinary fighting spirit at the 2026 Glasgow Commonwealth Games.

items.title: Govt seeks wider gas supply options as Malaysia moves to boost energy security
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 4 — The government is prioritising Malaysia’s energy security by diversifying access to large-scale gas resources that could broaden supply options and enhance the country’s energy resilience. The Economy Ministry said that amid uncertainty in global energy markets caused by geopolitical tensions, Malaysia remained focused on diversifying its energy supply sources to reduce reliance on any single country or market. Regarding opportunities to develop gas fields in Turkmenistan, the ministry said such ventures would be assessed based on their commercial merits and potential contribution to diversifying Malaysia’s long-term gas supply.

items.title: KTMB expands Southern Shuttle route linking Paloh to JB Sentral from Aug 8
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 4 — Keretapi Tanah Melayu Berhad (KTMB) will extend its Southern Shuttle service on the Paloh-JB Sentral-Paloh route from Aug 8. KTMB said in a statement yesterday that the expanded service will cover seven stations—Paloh, Kluang, Renggam, Layang-Layang, Kulai, Kempas Baru and JB Sentral—with the journey from Paloh to JB Sentral taking about 120 minutes. KTMB said the new service will operate 10 trips daily, comprising five services from Paloh to JB Sentral and five in the opposite direction, with each train accommodating up to 400 passengers.

items.title: Malaysia, Cambodia to strengthen cooperation in AI, digital economy and cross-border crime, says Anwar
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 4 — Malaysia and Cambodia have reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening strategic cooperation across various sectors, including the digital economy, artificial intelligence (AI), the halal industry, food security and human capital development, says Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. In a Facebook post last night he said the commitment also encompassed efforts to enhance cooperation in combating cross-border crime. Anwar said the matter was discussed during a courtesy call by Cambodian Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation Prak Sokhonn, who began a two-day official visit to Malaysia today.
